operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: 100 Days In, DRC Ebola Toll Hits 5,584 Cases as Africa CDC Warns True Burden Could Be 2-3x Higher
heroSubtitle: As the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak passed 100 days since its 15 May declaration, WHO's 23 August Situation Report #15 recorded 5,584 confirmed cases and 2,680 deaths (crude CFR ~48.0%) across 57 health zones in six provinces, including two newly affected zones (Viadana, Bas-Uélé; Mutwanga, North Kivu). Africa CDC officials warned on 22 August that official detection likely captures only 30-40% of true infections — meaning the real case burden could be 10,000-15,000 — and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026. A joint WHO/UN 100-day review found major response scale-up (testing labs from 1 to 19, treatment beds from under 10 to over 1,300, contact tracing from 9% to 84%), even as roughly 60% of weekly deaths continue occurring outside treatment centers. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic. The Washington Post reported 26 August that funding shortfalls and misinformation continue to hamper the response on the ground.
footerNote: Data sourced from DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE) situation reports, ECDC outbreak tracker, WHO Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC statements, Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, MSF, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Euronews, STAT News, and UN News. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
